harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a demo HTTP app on node2:8080 (RHEL7, systemd-managed python2 SimpleHTTPServer), reachable only from node1's LAN IP via a firewalld rich-rule. Configured a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 (VyOS, native kernel WireGuard, wg0=10.200.0.1/24) peered with node3 (RHEL7 3.10 kernel has no in-kernel WireGuard, so wireguard-go was built from source with Go 1.23 and run via wg-quick/wg-quick@wg0.service, wg0=10.200.0.2/24). node1 forwards and hairpin-SNATs traffic arriving on wg0 destined for node2:8080 to its own LAN IP, so node2 only ever sees connections sourced from node1 — enforcing that node3 can reach the app only through the tunnel. Verified direct node3->node2:8080 access is blocked while tunnel access succeeds (HTTP 200). All three nodes were restarted one at a time with the native reboot mechanism; boot_id changed on each; WireGuard tunnel, firewall/NAT config, and the app service all recovered automatically after each restart, with end-to-end tunnel access and the blocked-bypass property re-verified after all three restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1=VyOS with native kernel WireGuard, node2/node3=RHEL7 7.9 on a flat 10.100.6.0/24 network (isolation between node3 and node2 enforced via firewall+NAT since re-provisioning the cluster network was disallowed)

On node3: added CentOS-vault base/extras/updates repos, ELRepo, and archived EPEL repo (mirrorlist was dead); installed wireguard-tools, git, EPEL golang, then downloaded Go 1.23.4 tarball (EPEL's go1.20 couldn't parse the go.mod version format) and built wireguard-go from source since the 3.10 kernel has no WireGuard module
Generated WireGuard keypairs: node1 via VyOS PKI (run generate pki wireguard key-pair install interface wg0), node3 via wg genkey/pubkey

Configured node1 wg0 (10.200.0.1/24, UDP 51820, peer node3) in one atomic VyOS configure/commit/save session (had to combine address+port+key-generate+peer+commit in a single session because uncommitted VyOS sessions don't persist across exec calls)

Configured VyOS NAT source rule 100 (hairpin masquerade: src 10.200.0.0/24, dst 10.100.6.11, outbound eth0) and firewall ipv4 forward filter (default-action drop, rule 5 allow state established/related, rule 10 allow tcp/8080 from wg0 to 10.100.6.11) plus input filter allowing UDP/51820
Deployed demo-app.service (python2 SimpleHTTPServer on port 8080) on node2, enabled+started via systemd

Locked down node2 firewalld public zone with a rich-rule allowing tcp/8080 only from 10.100.6.10 (node1); confirmed the zone's implicit default-drop blocks all other sources without needing an explicit drop rule (explicit drop rules were tested and removed since old firewalld on RHEL7 doesn't support rich-rule priority ordering)

Configured node3 wg0.conf (address 10.200.0.2/24, peer node1 endpoint 10.100.6.10:51820, AllowedIPs 10.100.6.11/32) and brought it up via wg-quick with WG_QUICK_USERSPACE_IMPLEMENTATION=wireguard-go; installed a systemd drop-in on wg-quick@.service to set PATH and the userspace-implementation env var, then enabled wg-quick@wg0 for persistence

Verified end-to-end: node1->node2:8080 direct = 200; node3 direct bypass (eth0) = blocked/refused; node3 via wg0 tunnel = 200; conntrack on node1 showed the pre-NAT (10.200.0.2->10.100.6.11) and post-NAT (10.100.6.10->10.100.6.11) flow confirming the relay path

Captured boot_id baseline on all three nodes, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect), polled each until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id, and re-verified service/tunnel/firewall health and the tunnel-only access property after each restart before moving to the next node

evidence.requirement: App served from node2 on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: demo-app.service (python2 SimpleHTTPServer) enabled and active on node2, curl to 127.0.0.1:8080 returns the app content

evidence.requirement: node3 direct access to node2:8080 is blocked (not reachable except via tunnel)
evidence.summary: curl from node3 directly (and explicitly via eth0) to 10.100.6.11:8080 times out/connection-refused (000), both before and after all node restarts

evidence.requirement: node3 can reach node2:8080 through the WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
evidence.summary: curl from node3 over wg0 to 10.100.6.11:8080 returns HTTP 200 with the app body, confirmed initially and after every subsequent node restart

evidence.requirement: WireGuard tunnel correctly terminates on node1 and relays via NAT to node2
evidence.summary: wg show on node1 shows established handshake with node3 peer; VyOS NAT source rule 100 (hairpin masquerade) configured; conntrack shows pre-NAT (10.200.0.2->10.100.6.11) and post-NAT (10.100.6.10->10.100.6.11) entries for the same flow, proving the relay path

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebd78841... captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 84cc10ac... (changed); wg0/NAT/forward-filter config persisted via VyOS save; fresh WireGuard handshake and HTTP 200 through the tunnel confirmed after restart

evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 738d0aac... captured; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-restart boot_id 561c8dad... (changed); wg-quick@wg0.service active with fresh handshake, tunnel access to node2:8080 returns 200, direct bypass still blocked
